verdicts.flaw_description: The outcome is measured on a narrower population than the claim: "The counts cover the sessions that reached the new page" while "a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout", so a quarter of each segment is excluded from the current-period figures but is presumably in the earlier-month baseline the 4-7 percent gains are measured against. The discount confounder is neutralised (fixed-price contract catalogue), but the selected denominator is not.

Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the inhaler was started: group One "started 4 March, had 6 fewer attacks by 28 February" and group Three "started 5 September, had 7 fewer attacks by 30 August". The dates run backwards, so those reductions cannot be effects of the inhaler.

Per-protocol selection: "Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse", so the 9-16 degree gains are computed only on the adherent three-quarters, who would be expected to recover better anyway. (The corticosteroid rise is neutralised, since every intake was barred from injections.)

The defect rates "cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout" while "about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile", so roughly ten percent of each run - plausibly the reworked or problem boards - is dropped from the numerator and denominator, which alone could produce the 4-7 percent apparent reduction.
